event.title: Instructed Life Drawing – Gestural & Structural Approach to the Figure (18+, Beginner to Advanced Level)
event.description: “Students both beginning, intermediate and advanced can learn from Francesco’s excellent teaching methods, knowledge, humor, passion for the human form and all aspects of fine art. Students are fortunate to have an artist of his level as instructor.” This class is ideal for students of all levels, from beginners to advanced. Rather than copying, you’ll learn to see and draw by interpreting the figure through gesture, form, and structure. Each session begins with a 30-minute demonstration by Francesco, followed by 2.5 hours of drawing from a live model. Individual guidance and feedback are available throughout the class. Topics include: Gesture drawing fundamentals Building the figure with essential forms Using contour lines and landmarks for volume and perspective Understanding overlaps, foreshortening, and weight distribution Differentiating core and cast shadows Sighting techniques and simplified anatomy Whether you’re just starting or refining your figure drawing skills, Francesco’s instruction will help you grow with clarity and confidence. Supplies Needed: * 2 Charcoal pencils 2B * 1 White plastic eraser * 1 Kneaded eraser * 1 18″x 24″ Newsprint pad – 100 sheet * Blending stumps assorted sizes 4 pc. * No oils, solvent or fixatives are allowed in the class

event.title: Mend & Make New
event.description: Mend & Make New is a six‑week creative repair course that teaches students how to refresh, reinforce, and reimagine their clothing using both subtle and expressive techniques. Through invisible mending, visible patchwork, embroidery, darning, and hybrid redesign, students learn how to assess damage, choose the right materials, and build repairs that are both durable and personal. The class blends practical skill‑building with organic, discovery‑based learning while encouraging students to explore materials, experiment with stitches, and find their own style of repair. By the end of the series, each student completes a final project that combines multiple techniques and celebrates the character of well‑loved garments.

event.title: Paint Like Bob Ross: Ebb Tide
event.description: “Let’s build a happy little cloud. Let’s build some happy little trees.” – Bob Ross Join Mathew Halstead, CRI of Lazy Painter Brushworks, for a classic Bob Ross painting workshop with friends at the Alliance. event.title: The Quill: A Writers Circle
event.description: The Quill at Alliance for the Arts is a writers group with the goal of building a stronger creative writing community in Southwest Florida. event.title: October Galleries Opening Reception: Passage | Dahye Kim | Marian Fuller
event.description: On Display: October 2 – 31 Opening Reception: October 2nd, 5:00-7:00 p.m. Passage: A Themed Members Show We invite all Alliance member artists to submit one original work inspired by the theme “Passage” for exhibition in the main gallery during October 2026. The theme encourages both literal and abstract interpretations of transition, movement, transformation, and emotional or psychological change, from shifting seasons and aging to journeys through physical and symbolic spaces. Artists are also encouraged to explore unconventional approaches, including text-based works and mixed media incorporating poetry, prose, or fragmented narratives, while defining the theme through their own unique perspective. Submit Online (artinlee.org/passage): September 13th by 11:59 PM Call Details: Passage – Call Prospectus _____________________________________________________________ Foulds Theater Gallery Time no Time by Dahye Kim Ambiguous, intangible, and in flux, Dahye Kim’s installation explores time and memory as processes of becoming, dissolving, and re-emerging. Time no Time, her second solo exhibition in Florida, reflects on a reality increasingly mediated and reduced through technology and the online world. Drawn from photographs taken during her travels and thoughts developed over the past six years across diverse natural landscapes in the United States, the exhibition examines shifting perceptions of presence, memory, and temporality in digital space. As a conceptual digital media artist, Kim creates immersive environments using video, photography, internet, coding, light, and sound. Her practice investigates the intersections of time, memory, environment, and scientific ideas through technologically mediated experiences. In this exhibition, reflective screens function as temporal mirrors in which past, present, and future collapse into a continuous surface. Transforming the gallery into a fluid and shifting environment, Kim blurs the boundaries between material and immaterial, presence and illusion, and the natural and artificial. Minimal gestures—subtle color transitions, horizon-like lines, and shifting light—evoke unstable landscapes suspended between physical and virtual space. Her work gestures toward the evolving condition of the internet, where time fragments, loops, and becomes increasingly abstract. Through minimal digital interventions, Kim invites viewers to experience time not as linear, but as something sensed, elusive, and constantly unfolding. More on the artist: dahyekim.com _____________________________________________________________ Member Gallery Selected Works by Marian Fuller Marian Fuller’s mixed-media exhibition focuses on the beauty hidden within everyday life by transforming found and recycled materials into richly textured works that invite the viewer into a state of discovery. Inspired by neighborhood walks, international travel, thrift stores, and overlooked objects, she creates compositions that encourage viewers to look beyond the familiar and uncover unexpected meaning in ordinary things. Working with handmade paper, reclaimed materials, shredded credit cards, and other found objects, Fuller embraces experimentation and sustainability, allowing each piece to tell its own story through texture and layered details. Visitors are encouraged to experience the work up close, exploring the materials and subtle surprises woven throughout the collection while discovering the joy and adventure that define her creative process. _____________________________________________________________ Featured Artwork: “Corinthian Highway” by Kellen Beck Mills, “Time no Time” Digital Art by Dahye Kim (2020-2026) & “Item-7.13” by Marian Fuller

event.title: Autumn Magic: Witch’s Hat Wreath
event.description: Get into the Halloween spirit by creating a whimsical Witch’s Hat Wreath that’s sure to cast a spell on your front door! In this fun, hands-on workshop, participants will transform a simple wreath form into a festive witch’s hat using mesh, ribbon, florals, and seasonal embellishments. Learn easy wreath-making techniques, including layering, shaping, and securing decorative elements to create a full, eye-catching design. Whether your style is spooky, playful, or elegantly haunting, you’ll have the opportunity to customize your wreath with colors and accents that reflect your Halloween personality. All supplies are provided, so just bring your creativity and enjoy a relaxing, festive crafting experience. Each participant will leave with a beautiful handmade wreath that’s ready to welcome trick-or-treaters and celebrate the season in style.

event.title: Oil Painting Basics
event.description: Build confidence and develop your painting skills in this comprehensive 7-week oil painting course designed for both beginners and experienced artists. Whether you’re picking up a brush for the first time or looking to strengthen your technique, this class offers personalized instruction and guided exercises that will help you grow as a painter. Students will explore the essential materials, techniques, and principles of oil painting, including color mixing, composition, value, light, and brushwork. Through a variety of subjects—including still life, landscapes, self-portraits, and live models—you’ll learn to move beyond drawing what you think you see and begin painting from direct observation. This shift from symbolic thinking to perceptual seeing is the foundation for creating more accurate, expressive, and compelling paintings. By the end of the course, participants will have completed several original paintings, gained a solid understanding of oil painting fundamentals, and developed the confidence to continue painting independently. For the first 2 classes, we will be limiting our palette to black and white. Please bring: 1 LARGE tube white oil paint 1 LARGE tube black oil paint 1 PALETTE KNIFE the approximate size and shape of the one in the picture. I find the pointed tips easier to clean than the round tips. 1 OIL PAINTING BRUSH, size 10. I prefer synthetic brushes as they are easier to clean. I also prefer FILBERT brushes as the bristles are longer. 1 OIL PAINTING BRUSH, size 6. Synthetic/filbert. 1 PAPER PALETTE PAD. Disposable 1 PAD CANVAS PAPER, 10 sheets 1 ROLL PAPER TOWELS Instructor will provide odorless mineral spirits.

event.title: A Ghost Class- Sculpting with Jeff Ocasio
event.description: Gather with us for a ghostly afternoon of creativity as you sculpt your own friendly ghost. This class welcomes artists of all skill levels, whether you’re a beginner excited to explore your creative side or an experienced artist wanting to experiment with a new medium. Led by Jeff, whose relaxed and conversational teaching style encourages individual creativity, you’ll learn how to layer and manipulate masking tape using paper, wire, and glass marbles for the eyes to build a sturdy, free-standing ghost approximately 7 inches tall. At the end of class, you’ll take home your one-of-a-kind masking tape sculpture along with an instructional handout to help you seal and paint your artwork at home using easy-to-find materials. The class begins with a short tour of the artists’ studios inside DAAS CO-OP Gallery and The Union Artist Studios at the Arts & Eats Café. All supplies provided

event.title: Drawing Fundamentals (Ages 16+)
event.description: Discover the joy of drawing in this inspiring 7-week course designed for artists of every skill level. Whether you’re a complete beginner who thinks you can’t draw or an experienced artist looking to refresh your skills and see your work in a new way, this class offers a supportive and engaging environment to grow. Through guided exercises and personalized instruction, students will build confidence while developing essential drawing techniques, including observation, proportion, composition, value, and line quality. Working from a variety of subjects—including still lifes, landscapes, self-portraits, and live models—you’ll learn to move beyond drawing what you think you see and begin drawing what is actually in front of you. This shift from symbolic thinking to perceptual seeing is the foundation of accurate, expressive, and confident drawing. By the end of the seven weeks, you’ll have a stronger understanding of the fundamentals, improved observational skills, and the confidence to continue your artistic journey with a fresh perspective. Supplies: 2 Charcoal Pencils, 6B extra soft 2 White charcoal pencils OR White Compressed Charcoal Pencil sharpener Kneaded eraser Paper provided

event.title: Get Hooked: An Introduction to Crochet
event.description: In this fun and relaxed four-week series, you’ll discover the building blocks of crochet while creating a beginner-friendly fall pumpkin. This class is designed for anyone who has wanted to learn to crochet, no prior experience required. We’ll begin with the fundamentals, including yarn and hook basics, how to hold your materials, tension control, and the essential crochet techniques you’ll need to get started. You’ll learn how to create a slip knot and chain before progressing to basic crochet stitches as we work through the project together. Each session we’ll build on the previous weeks, giving you plenty of time to practice, ask questions, and receive hands on guidance along the way. By the end of the series, you’ll have completed your fall pumpkin and gained a foundation of skills you can continue to build on as you explore crochet on your own. Supplies needed: 5mm or 5.5mm crochet hook Medium weight acrylic yarn Body: orange, rust, cream, and other lighter fall themed colors (pick one) Stem: brown and green (pick one)

event.description: Strum, sing, and connect through music in this fun, welcoming group ukulele class for players of all levels. event.title: Picture Perfect: Exploring Photo Editing Techniques
event.description: You already take great photos with your camera or cell phone, but what happens after you press the shutter? With endless tutorials, YouTube videos, and AI tools at our fingertips, learning photo editing has never been more accessible. But there’s still tremendous value in sitting down with an experienced photographer who can help you understand not just how to edit, but why certain techniques work. Led by digital lab instructor and photographer Robert Ahrens, this session explores the evolving world of digital photo editing, from traditional editing techniques to the newest AI-powered tools found in today’s software and online platforms. Learn how to improve your images, streamline your editing workflow, and make thoughtful creative choices rather than simply relying on automatic corrections. We’ll also look at what you can do before you even press the shutter to give yourself a better image to work with later. Whether you’re photographing Florida wildlife, beaches, architecture, or our spectacular sunrises and sunsets, understanding the fundamentals of exposure, composition, resolution, and file quality can make a significant difference in your final results. This class is designed for everyone from the weekend photographer looking to sharpen their skills to semi-professional photographers and local realtors who want to create more polished, compelling images for their work. Bring your questions and curiosity and leave with new tools and techniques to take your photography to the next level.

event.title: Drawing Fundamentals (Ages 16+)
event.description: Discover the joy of drawing in this inspiring 7-week course designed for artists of every skill level. Whether you’re a complete beginner who thinks you can’t draw or an experienced artist looking to refresh your skills and see your work in a new way, this class offers a supportive and engaging environment to grow. Through guided exercises and personalized instruction, students will build confidence while developing essential drawing techniques, including observation, proportion, composition, value, and line quality. Working from a variety of subjects—including still lifes, landscapes, self-portraits, and live models—you’ll learn to move beyond drawing what you think you see and begin drawing what is actually in front of you. This shift from symbolic thinking to perceptual seeing is the foundation of accurate, expressive, and confident drawing. By the end of the seven weeks, you’ll have a stronger understanding of the fundamentals, improved observational skills, and the confidence to continue your artistic journey with a fresh perspective. Supplies: 2 Charcoal Pencils, 6B extra soft 2 White charcoal pencils OR White Compressed Charcoal Pencil sharpener Kneaded eraser Paper provided

event.title: Get Hooked: An Introduction to Crochet
event.description: In this fun and relaxed four-week series, you’ll discover the building blocks of crochet while creating a beginner-friendly fall pumpkin. This class is designed for anyone who has wanted to learn to crochet, no prior experience required. We’ll begin with the fundamentals, including yarn and hook basics, how to hold your materials, tension control, and the essential crochet techniques you’ll need to get started. You’ll learn how to create a slip knot and chain before progressing to basic crochet stitches as we work through the project together. Each session we’ll build on the previous weeks, giving you plenty of time to practice, ask questions, and receive hands on guidance along the way. By the end of the series, you’ll have completed your fall pumpkin and gained a foundation of skills you can continue to build on as you explore crochet on your own. Supplies needed: 5mm or 5.5mm crochet hook Medium weight acrylic yarn Body: orange, rust, cream, and other lighter fall themed colors (pick one) Stem: brown and green (pick one)

event.title: Contemporary Painting with Terry Lynn
event.description: Unlock your creativity in this engaging weekly painting class with beloved artist and instructor, Terry Lynn Spry! Designed for all skill levels—from beginners to seasoned professionals—this class allows students to work at their own pace with their preferred subject and medium. Explore a wide range of painting styles, from realism to abstract, while deepening your understanding of portraiture, color control, composition, value studies, and drawing techniques. With personalized guidance and a supportive environment, you’ll refine your skills and develop your artistic voice. Choose the best time of day for you: Morning- 9:30am-12:30pm Afternoon- 1pm-4pm Evening- 6:30pm-9pm Times available to choose in the registration process. Supply List: Paints: Alizarin Crimson Cadmium Red Cadmium Yellow Light Phthalo Blue Ultramarine Blue Ivory Black Titanium White Brushes: Filberts (Sizes 2, 4, 6, 8) Soft Synthetic Brushes A Few Large Bristle Brushes Palette Knife Miscellaneous: Paper Towels Container for Water (for acrylics) Sealed Container for Mineral Spirits (for oils) 9×12 Canvas Paper Pad Palette Paper, Freezer Paper, or Paper Plates

event.title: Drop In with Terry Lynn (All Levels)
event.description: Interested in taking a class with beloved Instructor Terry Lynn, but not sure you can make all the sessions? Wanting to try painting, but a little worried the class might be “over your head”? Then this is your big opportunity! Drop in and try one of Terry Lynn’s painting classes – Painting with Terry Lynn AM, Painting with Terry Lynn PM or Painting Studio with Terry Lynn – whichever time and whatever Tuesday works best for you! Students have the choice to bring in a painting they’ve been working on. Or they can take a color class, drawing class or choose something from the instructor’s materials. You may bring your own supplies (check supply list from Tuesday class) or purchase supply kit from the instructor for $20.

event.title: Group Ukulele Lessons
event.description: Strum, sing, and connect through music in this fun, welcoming group ukulele class for players of all levels. Whether you’re picking up an instrument for the first time or returning after a break, Amy Noel Walters will guide you through essential rhythm, chords, and technique in a way that’s supportive, creative, and confidence-building. Each class blends hands-on practice with clear, easy-to-follow instruction, helping you build a strong musical foundation while exploring songs you love. You’ll also discover simple ways to incorporate breath, mindfulness, and body awareness into your playing, making music not just something you play, but something you feel. Bring your instrument, your curiosity, and a smile because making music is better together. What to bring: Ukulele, tuner, water, and a notebook Supply fee of $15 due directly to the Instructor Single-class options available during the registration process. $30/members $35/non-members

event.title: Zentangle for the Seasons
event.description: Discover the Art of Zentangle: A Creative Journey Through the Seasons Unwind and unlock your inner artist with Zentangle—a simple, meditative method of drawing beautiful patterns one step at a time. Perfect for beginners, this class starts with the foundational techniques and gradually builds your confidence and creativity. Each week, you’ll create unique seasonal artworks that reflect the time of year, combining relaxation with artistic expression. No prior experience needed—just a willingness to explore, create, and enjoy the process! Supplies provided for a $10 fee due directly to the Instructor

event.title: Fine Art Acrylics with Marilyn Hedlund
event.description: Join artist Marilyn Hedlund for a dynamic, critique-based class designed to inspire artists of all levels. Each session begins and ends with lively group critiques where ideas, techniques, and feedback are shared freely in a supportive environment. Between critiques, you’ll work at your own station and pace, developing your artwork with personalized, one-on-one guidance from Marilyn. Expect to be challenged and inspired through stimulating discussions, creative assignments, and lecture/demos on essential topics like composition, form, color, and contrast. This is more than a class—it’s a creative community where fresh ideas, constructive critique, and artistic growth go hand in hand. Supply list: Paints – The quality of your paint may be the most important key to your success. Please don’t waste money on student or craft-grade paint. Recommended: Liquitex Fine Art Acrylic Heavy Body or Golden Acrylics You only need 6 colors: Ultramarine Blue Pthalo Blue (Green Shade) Cad Yellow Light Quinacradone Magenta Napthol Crimson Titanium White Brushes Bristle vs. synthetic sizes 1/2 ” to 2″9 Surfaces Bristol paper Canvas Panels, etc. Masking tape (not colored) Canvas Panels, etc. Paper: Bristol, acrylic, or watercolor If you use papers, you will need some kind of board or cardboard and clips Miscellaneous Roll of refrigerator/wax paper for palette White masking tape Various pens, pencils, charcoal, drawing tools Optional: notebook for taking notes

event.title: Instructed Life Drawing – Gestural & Structural Approach to the Figure (18+, Beginner to Advanced Level)
event.description: “Students both beginning, intermediate and advanced can learn from Francesco’s excellent teaching methods, knowledge, humor, passion for the human form and all aspects of fine art. Students are fortunate to have an artist of his level as instructor.” This class is ideal for students of all levels, from beginners to advanced. Rather than copying, you’ll learn to see and draw by interpreting the figure through gesture, form, and structure. Each session begins with a 30-minute demonstration by Francesco, followed by 2.5 hours of drawing from a live model. Individual guidance and feedback are available throughout the class. Topics include: Gesture drawing fundamentals Building the figure with essential forms Using contour lines and landmarks for volume and perspective Understanding overlaps, foreshortening, and weight distribution Differentiating core and cast shadows Sighting techniques and simplified anatomy Whether you’re just starting or refining your figure drawing skills, Francesco’s instruction will help you grow with clarity and confidence. Supplies Needed: * 2 Charcoal pencils 2B * 1 White plastic eraser * 1 Kneaded eraser * 1 18″x 24″ Newsprint pad – 100 sheet * Blending stumps assorted sizes 4 pc. * No oils, solvent or fixatives are allowed in the class

event.title: Hula Dance (Ages 3-12)
event.description: Experience the spirit and rhythm of the Pacific Islands in Hula with Marliss! This dynamic class introduces students to the traditional styles of Hawaiian, Tahitian, Māori, and Samoan dance. With a focus on both technique and cultural appreciation, students will learn the foundations of each style while mastering vibrant performance dances and songs. Throughout the year, students will have the opportunity to showcase their skills and celebrate Polynesian culture at 3-4 community performances. Costumes are required for performances and are provided at a minimal cost. Come dance, learn, and connect with the rich traditions of Polynesia in a fun and supportive environment! NO CLASS ON 11/11 (Veteran’s Day) OR 11/25 (Thanksgiving Break)

event.title: He Said, She Said: Writing Better Dialogue
event.description: Bad dialog is one of the surest signs of an amateur writer. In this course taught by award-winning novelist Roberto Calas, you’ll learn the subtle secrets of making the spoken word sing. Or written words that are spoken, sing. You get the point. Either way, readers will sing your praises with these helpful tips on dialog. We’ll take a deep dive into the world of character speech, covering a comprehensive array of categories including: Intrinsic vs. Extrinsic High Tension vs. Low Tension What lies beneath – Underspeak Characterization Through Dialog Slang and Jargon Expressive Lengthening Keep or Cut Dialog Tags (Optional) Bring five pages of a work in progress (containing dialog) for more personalized recommendations.

event.title: Life Drawing Lounge
event.description: Now on Wednesday evenings 6-9pm AND Sunday afternoons 1-4pm! Drop in, settle in, and draw! Life Drawing Lounge is a relaxed, non-instructed life drawing session featuring a nude model in one extended pose. Designed for artists of all levels with some basic life drawing experience, this is an opportunity to practice, experiment, and develop your skills in a casual, welcoming environment. Enjoy music, light conversation, and the freedom to work at your own pace. Artists are encouraged to bring and use the medium of their choice. $20 at the door No instruction provided

event.title: Mend & Make New
event.description: Mend & Make New is a six‑week creative repair course that teaches students how to refresh, reinforce, and reimagine their clothing using both subtle and expressive techniques. Through invisible mending, visible patchwork, embroidery, darning, and hybrid redesign, students learn how to assess damage, choose the right materials, and build repairs that are both durable and personal. The class blends practical skill‑building with organic, discovery‑based learning while encouraging students to explore materials, experiment with stitches, and find their own style of repair. By the end of the series, each student completes a final project that combines multiple techniques and celebrates the character of well‑loved garments.

event.title: Picture Perfect: Exploring Photo Editing Techniques
event.description: You already take great photos with your camera or cell phone, but what happens after you press the shutter? With endless tutorials, YouTube videos, and AI tools at our fingertips, learning photo editing has never been more accessible. But there’s still tremendous value in sitting down with an experienced photographer who can help you understand not just how to edit, but why certain techniques work. Led by digital lab instructor and photographer Robert Ahrens, this session explores the evolving world of digital photo editing, from traditional editing techniques to the newest AI-powered tools found in today’s software and online platforms. Learn how to improve your images, streamline your editing workflow, and make thoughtful creative choices rather than simply relying on automatic corrections. We’ll also look at what you can do before you even press the shutter to give yourself a better image to work with later. Whether you’re photographing Florida wildlife, beaches, architecture, or our spectacular sunrises and sunsets, understanding the fundamentals of exposure, composition, resolution, and file quality can make a significant difference in your final results. This class is designed for everyone from the weekend photographer looking to sharpen their skills to semi-professional photographers and local realtors who want to create more polished, compelling images for their work. Bring your questions and curiosity and leave with new tools and techniques to take your photography to the next level.

event.title: Watercolor with Linda Benson
event.description: Enjoy being creative with transparent watercolors. Linda Benson’s hands-on teaching technique allows you to create along with her in the classroom. Learn something new or refresh your skills. You will learn brush techniques, color theory, perspective, gradients, and composition. Each week is a new lesson complete with reference handouts. You will learn tricks that aren’t in the book and secrets for a successful painting. Supplies Needed: 6 Primary transparent watercolor tubes – any Red, Orange, Yellow, Green, Blue, Violet (traditional tube watercolors are transparent like Daniels, Holbein, & Windsor Newton, QoR, not opaque. Look for transparent tubes not round cakes) Watercolor brushes: Round and flat assortment with 1 inch flat 140 Lb. Watercolor paper or block 11×14 (Arches is good watercolor paper but Strathmore is OK if it is 140-pound stock) Watercolor pallet tray with cover Bring 2 water cups 1 roll of paper towels Small note book or mini sketch book Pencils Blue ballpoint pen Pencil erasers Carry bag Pencil case If you already have some supplies, bring in what you have and we will work with that. Linda will have some brushes and some supplies to share on the first day of class for beginners. Advanced students bring what you have.

event.title: Acrylic Painting with Pat Smelkoff: Large Sunflower
event.description: Bring a little sunshine to your canvas! In this fun and creative workshop, you’ll paint a large, vibrant sunflower using acrylic paints. With step-by-step guidance, you’ll explore color mixing, brush techniques, layering, and highlights as you bring your sunflower to life. Whether you’re an experienced painter or picking up a brush for the first time, this workshop is designed to be relaxed, approachable, and fun. Create a bold, beautiful piece of artwork that will brighten up your home—or make a wonderful gift! All supplies are provided

event.title: Art Without Rules: Teen MultiMedia Space (Age 13-18)
event.description: Step into a creative space where experimentation is encouraged and there’s no single “right” way to make art. In this ongoing studio-style class, teens will explore a wide range of materials and techniques while building confidence in their artistic voice. Each week introduces a new theme, artist, or source of inspiration, paired with guided mini-lessons that spark ideas and expand creative skills. Students will have the freedom to explore painting, drawing, mixed media, and more—while also continuing to develop personal projects over time. This class balances structure with creative freedom, helping teens strengthen foundational skills, discover new mediums, and grow as artists in a supportive, inspiring environment. Single sessions available for $25/member, attend one session, or all 5! $15 supply fee for full series OR $5/class for single sessions, paid directly to the Instructor

event.title: The Quill: A Writers Circle
event.description: The Quill at Alliance for the Arts is a writers group with the goal of building a stronger creative writing community in Southwest Florida. We are, primarily, a fiction critique group, but The Quill is also a place to practice your craft, learn new skills, network with other writers, and discuss all writing-related matters. The moderator–historical-fantasy author Roberto Calas–will maintain a safe, supportive space for all participants. All skill levels and genres are welcome. So, come have your work-in-progress critiqued. Try a quick creative writing exercise. Level-up your skills, and enjoy the company of your writing peers. Meeting the first and third Thursdays from 6:30 – 9pm of every month Free for Alliance Members, non Members are welcome for $5 at the door

event.title: Sip and Create: Fall Flower Fun
event.description: Celebrate the beauty of autumn by creating a one-of-a-kind floral vase using the timeless art of decoupage. In this relaxing, hands-on workshop, participants will embellish a glass vase with delicate pressed flowers, transforming it into a beautiful piece of functional art. As you slow down, create, and enjoy the process, you’ll learn simple decoupage techniques that are easy to recreate at home. Perfect for displaying fresh fall blooms or as a thoughtful handmade gift, your finished vase will bring warmth and beauty to your home throughout the season. All supplies are provided, including the vase, pressed flowers, decoupage materials, and finishing supplies. Each participant will leave with a completed keepsake vase and the satisfaction of creating something both beautiful and meaningful. Screenshot

event.title: Alliance Morning Market
event.description: The Alliance for the Arts has reimagined its community market experience with the launch of the Alliance Morning Artisan Market, a new monthly event held on the third Saturday of each month from 9 a.m. to 1 p.m. The shift moves the Alliance’s former Wednesday night market to a vibrant Saturday morning gathering designed to bring families, artists, and the community together for a full day of creativity and connection. The first Alliance Morning Market will take place Saturday, Feb. 21, 2026, on the Alliance’s 10-acre campus at 10091 McGregor Blvd. The market will feature a curated mix of artisans and vendors, local artists, and live entertainment, creating a welcoming, festival-style atmosphere for all ages. By moving the market to Saturdays, the Alliance is aligning it with two popular free programs already offered on campus: Free Family ArtLabs, held from 10 a.m. to 12 p.m., and Reel Families, Free Family Movie Screenings, beginning at noon. Together, these programs create a seamless day of activities centered on creativity, community, and family-friendly fun. “The Alliance Morning Market allows us to bring together so many of the things our community loves, local artists, creative experiences for kids, live entertainment, and time spent together,” said Alliance representative and organizer, Cat Flo. “It’s more than a market; it’s a full morning and afternoon of connection.” Admission to the Alliance Morning Market and all accompanying activities is free. While gallery admission is always free, a $5 suggested donation helps support the Alliance’s mission to keep arts programming accessible and affordable. Event: Alliance Morning Market, Indoors & Outdoors Date: Every Third Saturday Time: 9am–1pm Includes: Local Vendors | Live Entertainment | Family ArtLab | Free Family Movie For more information about the Alliance Morning Market or other Alliance programs, visit ArtInLee.org or call 239-939-2787. For vending opportunities contact Cat@artinlee.org.

event.title: Acrylic Painting with Pat Smelkoff: Beginning Zhostovo: Metal Tray
event.description: Discover the elegance and drama of the traditional Russian decorative technique known as Zhostovo in this multi-week painting series. Inspired by the beautifully hand-painted metal trays of Zhostovo painting, students will learn the signature “Russian Stroke” method used to create lush, dimensional floral designs set against rich, dark backgrounds. Throughout the series, you’ll build skills step by step — practicing brush control, double-loading techniques, blending, highlights, and shadow work — before applying your knowledge to design and completing your own decorative tray. We’ll explore traditional compositions, color harmony, and the bold contrast that makes this style so striking. Perfect for beginners ready to learn foundational stroke work as well as experienced painters wanting to expand their decorative painting repertoire. By the end of the course, you’ll leave with a beautifully painted tray and the confidence to continue exploring this timeless folk art tradition. All supplies are provided This class will meet twice- on 10/17 and 10/31

event.title: Oil Painting Basics
event.description: Build confidence and develop your painting skills in this comprehensive 7-week oil painting course designed for both beginners and experienced artists. Whether you’re picking up a brush for the first time or looking to strengthen your technique, this class offers personalized instruction and guided exercises that will help you grow as a painter. Students will explore the essential materials, techniques, and principles of oil painting, including color mixing, composition, value, light, and brushwork. Through a variety of subjects—including still life, landscapes, self-portraits, and live models—you’ll learn to move beyond drawing what you think you see and begin painting from direct observation. This shift from symbolic thinking to perceptual seeing is the foundation for creating more accurate, expressive, and compelling paintings. By the end of the course, participants will have completed several original paintings, gained a solid understanding of oil painting fundamentals, and developed the confidence to continue painting independently. For the first 2 classes, we will be limiting our palette to black and white.
